You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily｜Bessent Says Strait of Hormuz Deal Imminent; Dow and S&P Hit Fresh Record Highs; Circle, SanDisk, Western Digital Earnings Ahead (August 5, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Developments
September Rate-Hike Probability Falls to 58.4%; Markets Focus on Upcoming Data
According to CME FedWatch, the probability of the Fed keeping rates unchanged in September has risen to 41.6%, while the probability of a cumulative 25 bp hike has declined to 58.4%. By October, the probability of a cumulative 25 bp hike stands at 53.9%, and a 50 bp hike at 15.5%.
Markets continue to digest Chair Warsh’s earlier reaffirmation of the 2% inflation target and the associated policy-path uncertainty.
The sharp recent decline in oil prices has helped ease inflation concerns, yet employment data remains the key pricing anchor.
Market Impact : The marginal cooling of rate-hike expectations combined with lower oil prices provides near-term support for risk assets. Volatility is likely to persist until non-farm payrolls and other key data are released.
International Commodities
Bessent Says Strait of Hormuz Deal Imminent; Oil Continues Sharp Decline
US Treasury Secretary Bessent stated that a deal regarding the Strait of Hormuz could be reached on August 4 or 5. Secretary of State Rubio noted that negotiations have made progress but a final agreement has not yet been finalized.
According to sources, Iran has softened its stance, abandoning the demand for full control over two-way shipping and instead proposing to manage inbound vessels while retaining supervision and intervention rights over outbound traffic. Iran is also considering allowing European participation in mine-clearing operations.
Brent crude has fallen back below $80 as markets price in the prospect of the strait reopening.
Market Impact : Expectations of geopolitical de-escalation continue to compress the crude risk premium. Consecutive sharp declines in oil prices have significantly eased near-term inflation pressure. Actual deal implementation and restoration of shipping remain the core variables.
Macroeconomic Policy
White House Advances AI Framework, Excludes Open-Source Models; Jones Act Waiver May Be Extended
The White House voluntary AI safety-testing framework defines “covered frontier models” as closed-source models with the most advanced capabilities that pose national-security risks; open-source models are excluded. Details of the framework are not planned for public release.
The White House is expected to extend the Jones Act waiver to help ease gasoline price pressure; the current waiver expires on August 16.
Anthropic has signed another multi-billion-dollar compute procurement agreement.
Market Impact : Progress on the AI regulatory framework reduces longer-term uncertainty, though the exclusion of open-source models and lack of public details have drawn attention. Extension of the Jones Act waiver supports energy-supply stability expectations.
II. Market Recap
Commodities FX Performance (Real-time Update)
Spot Gold : ~$4,081/oz, +0.1%
Spot Silver : ~$60.0/oz, +0.23%
WTI Crude : ~$75.39/bbl, -0.51%
Brent Crude : ~$76.53/bbl, -0.36%
US Dollar Index (DXY) : ~99.85, modest fluctuation
Driver Analysis : Bessent’s statement that a deal is imminent further compressed the crude risk premium. WTI and Brent continued their sharp declines, meaningfully easing inflation concerns. Gold and silver showed mixed performance amid lower oil prices and improving risk appetite, with silver displaying greater elasticity. The asset linkage remains clear: geopolitical de-escalation → lower oil → cooling inflation expectations → marginal reduction in Fed hike bets → support for risk assets. Near-term commodity moves still depend heavily on actual deal implementation and restoration of shipping through the strait.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : ~$63,985, +0.91%
ETH : ~$1,863, +0.65%
Total Crypto Market Cap : ~$2.28 trillion
Liquidations (24h) : Total ~$204 million, of which shorts ~$137 million
Bitget BTC/USDT Liquidation Map : Current price around $63,985. Dense short liquidations are concentrated in the $64,500–$65,500 zone above; a breakout could trigger further short-covering. Larger long-liquidation pressure remains in the $62,000–$63,500 area below. Price is currently in a high-liquidation-density zone, implying elevated short-term volatility risk.
Spot ETF Flows : BTC spot ETFs recorded a net inflow of $170 million yesterday; current dynamic net inflow stands at $40 million.
Driver Analysis : Geopolitical de-escalation and the US tech rebound lifted risk appetite, allowing the crypto market to stabilize overall. BTC remained relatively resilient while ETH showed more limited elasticity. Liquidation volumes declined and long/short forces moved toward balance. ETF flows remain a key constraint on upside. Lower oil prices and cooling rate-hike expectations provide macro support; the near-term outlook is likely range-bound, with attention focused on transmission of the Strait of Hormuz deal outcome into sentiment.

Dow Jones : Closed at 54,085.88 (+1.71%), fresh all-time high

Performance Summary Driver Analysis : All three major US indexes rose on Tuesday, with the Dow and SP 500 both hitting fresh record highs. Semiconductors and memory were strong, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained more than 6%. Palantir’s significant earnings beat and nearly 30% surge became the focal point, while Intel, AMD and other chip names followed higher. Amazon pulled back modestly and Meta was roughly flat. The move was driven by geopolitical de-escalation plus AI-software earnings delivery. Hardware-software divergence eased and overall risk appetite improved markedly.
[...]
Event Overview : Intel shares rose nearly 11% on Tuesday, becoming one of the leaders in the semiconductor sector, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) gained more than 6%. Intel had long lagged peers in AI transformation and foundry progress; the rebound magnitude significantly exceeded that of Nvidia, AMD and other leaders. Market Interpretation : Geopolitical de-escalation expectations and AI-demand sentiment repair jointly drove capital back into the chip sector. As a previously oversold “laggard,” Intel offered higher elasticity. Markets began to reassess progress on advanced-process catch-up, foundry customer expansion and government-subsidy realization, with short-term trading attributes clearly strengthened. Investment Implication : The semiconductor cycle and downstream AI capital-expenditure cadence remain the core pricing factors. Intel’s rebound largely reflects sentiment repair and capital rotation; subsequent observation should center on actual customer ramp progress and whether foundry profitability improvement can support higher valuations.
[...]
3. Amazon (AMZN) – Modest Pullback; Market Cap Remains Elevated
[...]
Event Overview : Amazon shares fell approximately 2.3% on Tuesday, ending the prior consecutive advance. The company’s market capitalization had previously surpassed $3 trillion for the first time, and it had completed its full $50 billion investment in OpenAI. Market Interpretation : Against the backdrop of a strong rebound in tech and semiconductors, Amazon’s relative underperformance appears more a technical profit-taking after the earlier surge than a fundamental deterioration. Attention remains on the matching of AWS growth with capital expenditure, yet the OpenAI equity linkage and AI-infrastructure positioning logic are unchanged. Near-term capital has preferred higher-elasticity software and hardware names. Investment Implication : Whether cloud growth can continue to absorb higher capital-expenditure levels remains the key determinant of medium-term valuation space. After the market-cap breakthrough, digestion pace and subsequent guidance become more important.
[...]
